description: Cobalt is a chemical element with symbol Co and atomic number 27. It is found in the Earth's crust only in chemically combined form, except for small deposits in natural meteoric iron alloys. The free element produced by reductive smelting is a hard, lustrous, somewhat brittle, gray metal.
uses: Cobalt is primarily used in lithium-ion batteries and in the manufacture of magnetic, wear-resistant and high-strength alloys. Cobalt-based compounds give distinctive blue color to glass, ceramics, inks, paints and varnishes, and cobalt-60 is used as a radioactive tracer and for production of gamma rays. It is also used in the petroleum industry as a catalyst for refining crude oil to remove sulfur, and cobalt is the active center of cobalamins (Vitamin B12), an essential vitamin for all animals.
characteristics: Cobalt is a ferromagnetic metal with specific gravity of 8.9 and Curie temperature of 1,115 °C. It is a weakly reducing metal protected from oxidation by a passivating oxide film, and occurs as two crystallographic structures (hcp and fcc) with an ideal transition temperature of 450 °C. Cobalt has common oxidation states of +2 and +3, forms pink [Co(H2O)6]2+ complexes in water, and exists naturally as only one stable isotope, cobalt-59.
